hallName: The first hall · The Cassopolis Hall of Comparative Ovations
question: Did the joke lodge of 1846 ever have a real charter? Even the man who first wrote its story wasn’t sure.

start.text: The post that opened this case, on the first hall’s Facebook page: “Somebody lost a lodge.”
start.label: Read the post ›

start.text: Howard S. Rogers, History of Cass County, from 1825 to 1875 (1875), pp. 253–254. Read past the quotation, and watch the word “charter.”
Alfred Mathews, History of Cass County, Michigan (1882), p. 174, which prints the story again. Compare the two.

frompost.lead: Somebody lost a lodge. It was here.

photos.alt: Page 253 of Rogers’s 1875 History of Cass County, with the paragraphs on the 1846 lodge boxed in red.
photos.cap: Rogers, 1875, p. 253: the first printing of the 1846 lodge, as James M. Shepard told it.

photos.alt: Page 254 of Rogers’s 1875 History of Cass County, the end of the lodge story boxed in red.
photos.cap: Rogers, p. 254. Just below the box: “the charter (?) members.” There is the question mark.

photos.alt: Page 174 of Mathews’s 1882 History of Cass County, Michigan, the lodge story under its own heading.
photos.cap: Mathews, 1882, p. 174: the same story seven years later. The question mark is gone.
